adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in handleNewBooking.ts lines 1871-1876, when creating a booking, only the first destination calendar is connected via `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`. The diff shows that `evt.destinationCalendar` is now an array (changed from single object to array throughout the codebase), and for collective team events, multiple destination calendars are pushed to this array (line 1068: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`). However, when persisting to the database, only the first element is saved. This means secondary host destination calendars are lost in the database, even though they were used for creating calendar events. Later flows that reload from the database will only have access to the first destination calendar, not the full array that was used during booking creation.
